turn.user_message: How does the day change on the wards?
turn.context: Prompt 1 of bm-au-07. bed-management.md §7.4.2 (allocate forward, admissions alongside discharges, 24-hour signal, 1 PM ICU signal, 5 PM round) and §7.4.1 (2 PM pass, 6 PM freeze, call-in times). Nagpur times from transcript 9 to 13.

transcript.label: After transcript turn 31 · Processes, turn 1 (the record stops at 31)

text: The work stays the same. What changes is when things are decided, so a bed is given before it is free.
bullets: Today a bed is given out only once it is clean. Your patients reach a bed between 4:30 and 8 PM.
In the new day, admissions run alongside the morning discharges. Each patient is called in for a set time.
Six times are fixed each day. They fix when a decision is made, never what the doctor decides.
chat.invite: Next, we can see where on the ward each change happens.
chat.note: Same people, same beds. A different order.
prompts: Where on the ward does each change happen?
Why do our patients still get in so late?
What does a doctor have to do?
chat.pointer: Switch between today and the new day. Pick a time to move the clock hand.

blocks.title: Same work, a different clock
blocks.deck: The ward’s day from 8 AM to 8 PM. Switch to set today’s admissions against the new ones.

switch.cap_today: Bills close by noon. Patients arrive at 1 PM and reach a bed from 4:30 PM.
switch.cap_with: Admissions run with the morning discharges. Patients reach a bed by about noon.

blocks.times_label: Fixed times of the new day
blocks.caption: Arrival at 1 PM and a bed from 4:30 PM are your times. The new times are the plan, not yet tried.

sheets.title: Admissions start with discharges
sheets.text: The desk starts admitting while the morning discharges run. It admits into beds that will be free, not beds already free.
sheets.entry: Who works the desk at 9 AM today?

sheets.title: Dates checked on the round
sheets.text: On the morning round the doctor sees a likely discharge date for each patient. They confirm it or change it, a day ahead.
sheets.entry: When does your morning round end?

sheets.title: Admissions done
sheets.text: Patients called in for a set time are in bed by about noon. The bill on their bed opens hours earlier.

lines.label: Today
lines.value: In bed 4:30 PM, up to 8 PM

sheets.entry: What time do most patients reach a bed today?

sheets.title: ICU step-down signal
sheets.text: ICU patients likely to move to a ward are named by 1 PM. That lets the 2 PM plan count their ICU beds.

lines.label: Who
lines.value: ICU in-charge and the treating doctor

sheets.entry: Who decides step-downs in your ICU today?

sheets.title: First bed plan
sheets.text: The first pass matches tomorrow’s planned patients to beds. Teams are told at once what still has no bed.

lines.label: Made by
lines.value: Tojo, checked by the Bed Manager

sheets.entry: How many planned admissions on a usual day?

sheets.title: The 5 PM round
sheets.text: One round of the beds likely to free tomorrow. Each date is confirmed or corrected by 5 PM.

sheets.title: Bed plan frozen
sheets.text: Tomorrow’s plan is frozen and sent to everyone. Each planned patient gets a call-in time for their bed.
sheets.entry: Who should get the 6 PM plan?

blocks.label: Patient in bed
blocks.sub: Each bed starts earning about four hours earlier. Nothing else about the stay changes.
